Vanessa — reviewed HelioTech_Redlines_20261201.docx and SOW_v3_redline.pdf. Short summary and recommended path:

What they ask that is high risk:
- Broad indemnity for IP and third-party data claims that is not limited to direct damages; they also want exceptions that could expose us to consequential damages tied to data processing.
- Removal of cap for breach scenarios — effectively unlimited exposure.

Recommended redlines (legal):
1) Keep indemnity narrow: Redwood indemnifies for direct IP infringement where Redwood-provided models/code are the proximate cause; defend + indemnify for amounts awarded. Exclude contractual indemnities for customer data misuse where customer controls ingestion.
2) Liability cap: cap overall liability at 2x fees paid in prior 12 months (or $2M, whichever is greater) — carve out for willful misconduct and gross negligence only. Do not accept unlimited breach cap.
3) Warranty: limit to that the service will conform materially to the documentation and that we will use commercially reasonable security practices; disclaim consequential damages.
4) Commercial concession: for strategic accounts, recommend a commercial discount up to 55% first-year on prepay, with a mandatory insurance requirement (E&O/Tech liability at least $5M) and SOC 2 Type II evidence.

Decision authority note: any amendment that removes the liability cap entirely or accepts open-ended indemnity requires CEO sign-off per policy. Anything within 2x fees + 55% discount is approvable by CRO/Sales leadership.

I can draft redline language that implements the above. If Sales is pushing for 65% & no cap, escalate to Aditya for final approval.

-Markus

Aditya — quick ask and one-pager summary below. I need a sign-off or explicit veto so we can move the counter to HelioTech.

Summary: HelioTech (potential ARR $1.8M FY1; expansion possible). They proposed 65% first-year discount + redlines that would broaden indemnity and remove liability cap. Legal (Markus) recommends we counter with: 2x fees liability cap, narrowed indemnity, warranty limited to documentation + commercially reasonable security practices, require E&O coverage ($5M min) and SOC 2 evidence. Sales recommends up to 55% discount for prepay if we accept the above legal protections.

Why this needs senior sign-off: HelioTech initially asked for removal of any liability cap for breach scenarios and broader indemnity language — accepting either would exceed the standard authority matrix and materially increase our tail risk.

Requested decision (pick one):
A) Approve Sales/Legal compromise: 55% first-year discount on annual prepay + legal redlines (2x fees cap, warranty language, insurance requirement).
B) Approve full commercial ask (65% + HelioTech redlines) — if yes, we will document rationale and exposure and require Executive Counsel to sign.
C) Decline and hold standard terms; offer a 45% pilot discount and shorter-term SOW.

Attachments: HelioTech_Redlines_20261201.docx, SOW_v3_redline.pdf. HubSpot: HT-2026-784. DocuSign candidate envelope linked below.

Please advise. We are on a tight timeline — HelioTech asked for a counter by Friday.

Team — thanks for the clear summary. I approve option A with two hard conditions and one ask:

Approved: Sales may proceed with a counter that offers up to 55% first-year discount on annual prepay, provided Legal inserts the following and we obtain evidence before contract execution:
1) Liability cap at 2x fees paid in the previous 12 months (explicit carve-out: willful misconduct & gross negligence). No unlimited breach carve-out.
2) Indemnity limited to direct IP infringement attributable to Redwood deliverables; exclude customer-controlled data ingestion scenarios.
3) Mandatory customer insurance: E&O/Tech liability $5M minimum, naming Redwood as additional insured for the SOW.

Additionally: require a SOC 2 Type II report or equivalent security questionnaire completed and ownership/controls documented prior to production. If HelioTech cannot meet the insurance/SOC 2 requirements, we pause and revert to a reduced pilot offer (45% discount, 6-month term).

I do NOT approve 65% + open indemnity. If Sales wants to push further, get explicit CEO sign-off with full risk memo; I will sign off only after legal quantifies exposure and Finance models expected loss scenarios.

GO: Ben/Vanessa — prepare the counter with Markus' redlines and the insurance/SOC 2 checklist, get DocuSign prepared, and close by Friday if possible.

— Aditya
